utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we are all here. Mr. Registrar, good afternoon. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good, Your Honour. This is Case Number IT-95-13/1PT, the Prosecutor versus Mile Mrksic, Miroslav Radic, and Veselin Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Mrksic, can you follow the proceedings in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MRKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Same question to you, Mr. Radic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED RADIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. Yes, I can follow the proceedings, too, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. Finally, Mr. Sljivancanin, good afternoon to you. Same question to you: Can you follow the proceedings in a language you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SLJIVANCANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I can follow the proceedings. Everything is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Jan Wubben, senior trial attorney for the Prosecution, together with Ms. Joanne Richardson and Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink, case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you and good afternoon to you and your team. Appearances for Accused Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour, on behalf of Milo Mrksic, Attorney Miroslav Vasic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Appearances for Accused Radic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Mr. Radic will be represented by Mr. Borivoje Borovic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And finally appearances for Veselin Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour, Mr. Sljivancanin shall be represented by Mr. Novak Lukic from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you all and good afternoon to you. Let's go through the usual routine which is a formality more than anything else. You are used to it but members of the public may not be. I'm going to explain the reasons for the Status Conference. First of all I wish to confirm that the last Status Conference in this case was held on the 11th of June, 2004. The Trial Chamber is required pursuant to Rule 65 bis to hold a Status Conference within 120 days after the previous one. So we are in time -- we are within the 120 days' limit. The purpose of this and other similar Status Conferences is to organise exchanges between the parties so as to ensure an expeditious preparation for trial. And then in addition, and this is a very important purpose of -- aim of this Status Conference, is to allow the accused to raise issues in relation to his or her mental and physical condition as well as to matters related to detention. In preparation for this particular Status Conference, a meeting within the terms pursuant to Rule 65 ter (D) was held between the parties and the Chamber's senior legal officer, Mr. Von Hebel on Wednesday, 6th October, at 1500 hours, that's yesterday, I understand -- at least I am informed that due to a delay in the arrival of the plane, counsel for Accused Mrksic was unable to be present; however, he agreed that the meeting could go on in his absence, for which I am thankful, for which I am thankful. I just want to know whether you have been briefed on what happened actually during the 65 ter meeting, Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Even before the meeting I had a meeting with my colleagues and we did determine the request the Defence would be making at the meeting pursuant to Rule 65 ter. And I see that these requests for made at the meeting. After the meeting my colleagues informed me of what was discussed at the meeting. So I am familiar with everything that was discussed at the meeting that was held pursuant to Rule 65 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Vasic. So move to the next point on the agenda which is outstanding motions. We are all aware that the Defence challenged the form of the indictment. When I say "the Defence," it's a relative statement in that only the Accused Mrksic and Sljivancanin did so. On the 20th of July of this year, the Trial Chamber issued its decision on the form of modified consolidated amended indictment in which it allowed in part the preliminary motions of Accused Mrksic and Sljivancanin and directed the Prosecution to file an amended indictment. Am I going too fast for the interpreters or you can catch up? Okay. Thank you. The Prosecution subsequently filed its second modified consolidated amended indictment on the 26th of August. And on the 20th and on the 24th of September respectively counsel for Sljivancanin and for Mrksic filed preliminary motions alleging defects in the form of the latest indictment. This was as, is usual, the practice served on the Prosecution, and the Prosecution responded on the 4th of October, that is three days ago. We are in a position to issue a decision within a relatively short time, but before adjourning this matter for judgement I wanted to make sure that you do not have any further submissions to make, particularly the members of the Defence team that are interested in this matter that have seen the reply of the Prosecution, the reply of the Prosecution. Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have received the Prosecution's response, and I believe that the reasons set forth by Mr. Mile Mrksic's Defence in its preliminary motion still have good cause. And it is my opinion that in the new indictment issued by the Prosecution, although it has been amended, it still fails to specify all the elements it should have specified according to the decision rendered by the Trial Chamber. And there is nothing else that I would like to add. I quite simply think that not everything was specified as it should have been in accordance with the Trial Chamber's decision. Not all the parts were clarified by the Prosecution with regard to the objection raised by the Defence. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And, Mr. Lukic, if you have any comments. Because if you don't, you just have I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Matters are clear. I don't have any comments to make, and I'm not asking for a time limit to express my position with regard to what the Prosecution stated on the 4th of October, 2004. There is nothing I would like to comment on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, Mr. Lukic. I don't suppose you have anything to add, Mr. Wubben?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. So the understanding is, Mr. Von Hebel, that we start working on this decision in which we hope to be able to hand down to you very shortly. To my knowledge there are no further outstanding motions to be determined by the Trial Chamber, which prompts me to address the next item on the agenda which is disclosures. I am going to move from one type of disclosure to another. And as we go along what I will stop and ask for a confirmation of what I will be saying. I will start first with Rule 66(A)(i), material. The information that I have is that this chapter has been concluded. I just wanted to have a confirmation of this from the Defence and from the Prosecution. If -- you need only raise -- rise if it hasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, on behalf of all the Defence, I will say that everything was done in accordance with the rule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So I don't even need to address you, Mr. Wubben. And then we come to Rule 66(A)(ii), statements. You will recall -- I'm just trying to refresh my own and also everybody else's memory. You will recall that the question of this type of disclosure was raised in the course of the last Status Conference in June. At the time it transpired that the Prosecution had disclosed a 31 out of a total of 53 statements of witnesses expected to be called by the Prosecution. The Prosecution at the time added or made a statement to the effect that they expected to add a few witnesses from amongst those who were testifying at the time in the Ovcara trial then taking place in Serbia. I recall that in general the issue of translation of disclosed documents under Rule 66 and also Rule 68 was raised and submitted to the trial -- to me as the Pre-Trial Judge as something that was critical at the time. I will now tell you what according to the information I have, have been the developments. Then tell me if you agree or whether there are any developments I have not been aware of or whether there is any further information that I should receive. Since then the Prosecution has filed a partially confidential Prosecution's report concerning disclosure. This was filed on the 9th of August. I take it that you have received a copy of it. If not, please draw my attention to it. And the Prosecution, according to this report, has now disclosed the statement of 40 witnesses, of about 40 witnesses it intends to call at trial, whilst for the rest of them it will be requesting protective measures. This is the position as it emerges from the report. To my knowledge, the Defence argued that they do not know which of these witnesses whose statements have been disclosed will be called at trial. During the 65 ter meeting the senior legal officer asked the Prosecution to provide the Defence with a list of all the statements that have been disclosed to the Defence indicated which of those should at least provisionally be regarded as witnesses that will appear at trial and to copy the Pre-Trial Judge into it. So I take it this is a correct report that I have received, and if there is nothing forthcoming from the Prosecution, I would suggest that they could file the appropriate document if possible within seven days, if that is acceptable. Yes, Mr. Wubben, I see you --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Seven up to ten days -- sorry. Sorry, Your Honour. And I should raise. It was as I understood seven to ten days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And we would be glad to take that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Can you live with ten days. So you have ten days from -- I am actually giving you 11 days. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Because the 65 ter meeting was yesterday so it should be nine. I am still giving you ten. Ten starting from today, Mr. Wubben. I know that you do your level best to cooperate with the Tribunal. So within ten days from today from today, we shall be expecting a list indicating which of those witness statements fall under Rule 66(A)(ii) and which under Rule 68. We need to know that. That is an undertaking on your part. Then we have -- are there any further comments on Rule 66(A)(ii) disclosures. Yes, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. On behalf of all the Defence teams, I would like to state something that we discussed to an extent at the 65 ter meeting. So far we have only had nine statements pursuant to 66(A)(ii). As far as Rule 68, either (A) or (B), is concerned, what the Prosecution has stated we haven't received the central -- the main statements that they were supposed to provide us with. What does Rule 66(A) mean as far as witnesses are concerned out of the 31 statements that were provided according to Rule 68? And at the last Status Conference the Prosecution claimed that these statements were statements on witnesses who -- by witnesses who would be heard under Rule 66(A)(ii). These are statements given by witnesses to organs in Serbia and Montenegro. We don't know whether these witnesses have been heard by the Prosecution, have been questioned by the Prosecution. At the 65 ter meeting yesterday we, quite by chance, mentioned that -- and we found out with regard to a case in Belgrade, the Ovcara case, we found out that certain witnesses -- people cooperating were heard by the Prosecution. And in order to cooperate correctly in the future we asked that those statements they provided as protected witnesses or witnesses who were cooperating, we asked that they should provide these statements to the Defence. The Prosecution said that from the list of the 33 people who should be witnesses, we asked them to tell us which names they should disclose to us. We've only been provided with Petkovic and Jaskovic [phoen]. We don't know about the other names. We don't know which witnesses will be testifying from that case here as Prosecution witnesses. I apologise. I was speaking a little too rapidly. Perhaps the interpreters are finding it a little difficult to keep up. I think that a lot of time has passed, so from April of last year until today we have only received nine statements pursuant to Rule 66(A)(ii). Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wubben, do you have any comments on what has just been stated by Mr. Borovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. Yesterday at the 65 ter conference we had been triggered by this questions and Ms. Joanne Richardson will answer them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. In response to what was just raised by the Defence as the Office of the Prosecution speaking with at least two witnesses and -- to the charge that we have not turned these statements over, with respect to at least one witness we can verify that we indeed did not speak with him; we made attempts to. And we were prevented from the -- by the authorities in Belgrade from speaking with this witness because he had not testified yet in their trial, and they felt that this would compromise their proceedings. So we are also required to abide by the rules of procedure in Serbia. And as soon as we are able and are allowed access to these witnesses, we will indeed turn over a statement as soon as we have them. And if there are any questions from the Defence that there are other witnesses that are contending -- sometimes these contentions are based in rumour and not fact, they can contact us and we can certainly verify whether or not this is true. There is no reason why we can't informally address these matters. With respect to the statements that were turned over, we, the Prosecution, had sought to provide the statements that were given to us from the Ovcara proceedings to the Defence as quickly as possible to enable them to review the statements and to prepare. We acknowledge that we have not spoken to all of these individuals, but it was in our earnest approach to this matter that we wanted them to have the statements as soon as possible and so we labelled them as 66(A)(ii). And we anticipated as well that there would be some 68 material in them, because of course the trial in Belgrade may present conflicting theories with what is being presented here. So it was really in our attempt to accommodate the Defence that these statements were turned over to them. And we will, as we promised yesterday at the 65 ter, provide them with a list where we will more accurately indicate which witnesses we anticipate we will be calling. But keeping in mind, of course, this is only based on what to date we have been able to assess. And that the -- if there are any other witnesses who are not listed as 66(A)(ii), and we have turned over those statements, the Defence needs to keep in mind that we may very well at a later date change that assessment and indicate that they will be testifying on behalf of the Prosecution once we have spoken to them. So it's now a matter of bringing -- giving the Defence an updated statement, simply giving them a better indication of the exact witnesses we know to this point that we will be calling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That's very helpful indeed and helps to clarify a little bit the position. I did notice as well that we had -- the discussion turned also on Rule 68 material disclosure which I am going to address now. Basically in the partially confidential Prosecution fourth report concerning disclosure of the 9th of August that I referred to earlier, the matter of 68 disclosure is dealt with. And as a pre-trial Judge I have taken due notice of what is contained in that report. I remind you that at the time of the last Status Conference it appeared to me at least - correct me if I'm wrong - that 75 documents and 14 statements from witnesses from the Ovcara trial currently taking place in Serbia had been disclosed to the Defence in terms of -- pursuant to Rule 68. I think we -- I have confirmed this. If I am not correct, please correct me. Now I also --

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I also take it that during yesterday's 65 ter meeting you continued discussing the ongoing process of Rule 68 material disclosure, that you were encouraged -- that there were some problems at the moment relating to procuring such information from the Ovcara which you have helped clarify. These difficulties are perfectly understandable. They are not capriciously -- capricious or self-inflicted. So I reiterate the encouragement or the words of exaltation that my senior legal officer made yesterday. I encourage you to continue cooperating. I am sure that there is goodwill on the part of the Prosecution and that there should not be any difficulties along the way for further disclosure of whatever Rule 68 material emerges or surfaces. Are there any further comments on Rule 68 material disclosure? Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. As for Rule 68 I also hope that my learned friends will continue to carry out their obligations and that their database in this case will receive priority. We heard an explanation a few minutes ago about the obligation of the Prosecution to tell us which witnesses will be included according to Rule 68 and Rule 66(A)(ii) respectively. I just wish to add another problem, and believe that in this way we could speed things up and prevent any further problems from cropping up in these proceedings. When speaking of witnesses whose statements were disclosed to the Defence according to Rule 66(A)(ii) and who will be called as Prosecution witnesses, could they provide to the Defence all the statements that they have available right now. I believe that this is in the spirit of Rule 66(A)(ii) and on the other hand the Defence will have enough time to prepare. Also could we please have a list of all the proceedings that these witnesses took part in and also all the persons who interviewed them, the police, various authorities, and so on and so forth. The Prosecution knows this best of all, so could we please have all these witness statements of each and every one of these witnesses, all of those that were disclosed to the Defence according to Rule 66(A)(ii).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vasic. Is there feedback from Mr. Wubben or from Ms. Richardson?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it a request that you can comfortably meet or does it create problems for you?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: We will try to accommodate Defence. We will not at this time make any promises with respect to all of the statements. A number of these witnesses have testified before this Tribunal. They have testified before the military tribunal in Belgrade, and some of them are yet again testifying in Ovcara. Some have spoken to police officers in Serbia at different times. We will do all within our power to provide them with what we have. There are ISU searches that have not been completed because we are low on the priority, list of priorities before the Tribunal, and so we are somewhat limited in what we can provide. But whatever is in our possession with respect to the various statements that these witnesses may have made we will provide to them. And with respect to where these statements came from, we may or may not be able to provide that information. But we will certainly consider it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. Again, I think we ought to liaise and keep contact with each other -- with one another on this and see if you can meet halfway or reach an agreement. Any further observations on Rule 68 disclosure? No. Let's move fast. It looks as if we are moving ahead in a way which would lead us to a trial sooner than we thought. I can't tell you the exact date of the trial, but it is anticipated that the trial will start either early in 2005 or in mid-2005, early summer of 2005. So -- unless we get hitches, but it seems that we can plan for a trial to be held on that -- in that time frame. This is a matter now that I am going to touch upon in which I usually get involved -- I prefer to get involved the least possible. But I do make accommodation and that is with regard to agreed facts. I know that Mr. Von Hebel encouraged you to start the process of seeking to discuss amongst yourself and between yourselves the possibility of reaching agreement on a number of facts, which usually, if it happens at all, is a very helpful tool in the hands of the Trial Chamber and also in the hands of the parties because it cuts down on time which can then be made use of more profitably for the proper Prosecution or the proper Defence as the case may be. So I repeat the exaltation. I, too, recommend to you to start discussing the possibility of reaching agreement on certain facts. This is contemplated, as you know, in the rules and you are encouraged to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. follow that road. I am informed and I was very happy to read this, the senior legal officer's report, that the Defence showed an interest in getting this process started. So please go ahead. But as I said, the Trial Chamber cannot help you here and will not -- I as a pre-trial Judge will not interfere or intervene in this process. Now, before I come to the final part of the Status Conference are there any other matters that any one of you, Prosecution and Defence, would wish to raise? I start with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would like to accommodate this Trial Chamber with cooperation on agreed facts. We will -- may take some weeks before -- first we want to address the list and statement of witnesses and after that's done, we will take up this contact and we will be pleased to cooperate with Defence counsels further on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben. Mr. Vasic, starting with you. You happen to be the nearest. Do you have any other matters that you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to thank my learned friend and I believe that this is the right path to take. We hope that we will make headway with regard to agreed facts. We expect the Prosecution to give us their proposals and then we're going to respond to that. Could we please move into private session for a moment, because a question I would like to deal with has to do with the strategy of preparing the Defence and perhaps it would be easier to deal with it in private session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There's no objection on your part, Mr. Wubben?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we are agreed. You will have -- let me have a copy of all this correspondence. I take it there are no further matters that you would like to raise, neither the Prosecution nor the Defence which basically brings me to the last part of the Status Conference, which again might appear as a formality but which I do not consider as a formality. I consider it as a responsibility, as a duty, on my part. I'm going to address you, Mr. Mrksic, first. Would you like to raise any matter that is related to your state of health.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MRKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MRKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything is fine. I have no questions to raise. For the time being my health is relatively good. I hope that it will remain so until the trial begins.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I hope so, Mr. Mrksic. Do you wish to address me on any matter that may be related to your state of detention in the Detention Unit?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MRKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't hear the interpretation now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I will repeat the question. Do you wish to address me on matters related to your state of detention? Is everything going fine for you at the unit, at the Detention Unit, or not?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MRKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything is fine as far as the Detention Unit is concerned, if that was your question. I have no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You may sit down. Mr. Radic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED RADIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I also have no objections. Everything is fine for the time being. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That includes your health as well, I take it? Thank you, Mr. Radic. Mr. Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SLJIVANCANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no objections with regard to the Detention Unit. I still don't feel well, though, and I feel this length of time that I'm spending in prison waiting to be an encumbrance because I feel I'm innocent. So could you please do your best that this trial starts as soon as possible so that we finally hear the truth about this Ovcara that has been discussed for so long. Let justice finally be done and let the truth be heard. My attorney, Mr. Lukic, is trial-ready at this moment. We are prepared to begin. That is what I wish to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Sljivancanin. We will do our best. You know hat we can only hold six trials at a maximum at any one time. And while six trials are all going, we can't start the seventh. And there are other trials also that will need to start before yours. But as I said, the trial -- my Trial Chamber is doing its level best to make sure that this trial goes -- starts at the earliest -- as early possible. If we are lucky, it will start in the beginning of 2005 which is not very far away from us. I thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SLJIVANCANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That brings us to the end. The Status Conference -- I declare the Status Conference closed and we therefore stand adjourned. The next Status Conference will be convened according to the rules. Thank you and good afternoon to everyone. ---Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at 3.58 p.m. 24
